narrative:

The figure stands in a mountain stream. On the top of a cliff to the left of the picture is a salamander. On a cliff to the right of the picture are two eagles in a nest. The elements of One and Two are present. To offer SHELTER to those in need is a commendable act. Even when you have little yourself you tend to offer what you have, to help those even 1I8 Egg Suit less fortunate.

This is a wonderful trait but you need to be slightly more circumspect. There are many who would take advantage of your good nature, to your detriment. It is this that gives you much of your strength.

You are, or should be, very open with no prejudice, no bigotry, no antagonism of any sort toward others. The salamander is the fire from which will come new birth; a new beginning, That fire may be a low heat or of a high intensity. So may run your feelings: soft and low, or fierce and hot. You need to be more aware of your feelings, and your reactions to people and situations. If you have a temper that can become quickly inflamed, learn to assuage it and bring it under control. description: Mercurius senex, the Saturnian old man, reclines while exhaling spiritus and anima as two angels. A raven of the nigredo perches on him. Old man, angels, and raven are enclosed within the protective egg, womb, or alembic. Outside, Sol radiates intense heat while Wind or Aeolus blows in opposition. Above appear the Sun, Moon, Venus, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn.
narrative:
secure topaz 8: SECURE

Keyword: Secure. Gifts: Security. Gratitude. Serenity. Inner balance. Freedom from fear. Challenges: Resolving inner conflicts. Overcoming loneliness. Showing appreciation. The illustration is from the Viatorium Spagyricum of Herbrandt Jamsthaler (Frankfort on the Main, 1625).

The picture shows the image of Mercurius senex exhaling the spiritus and anima, or spirit and soul, in the form of angels. Mercurius senex is Saturn, in alchemy representative of "moist" vapors (combining with the "dry" vapors of sulphur, the Greeks and later followers believed these to be the composition of all metals). The raven, symbol of the nigredo, is perched on the old man. Nigredo, or blackness, is the initial state of the substance, in alchemy. The figures are enclosed in the protective egg; the 130 Egg Suit womb or alembic.

Outside the egg are the opposing forces of Sun/Sol (radiating immense heat) and Wind/Aolus (blowing with full force). Above are the Sun, Moon, Venus, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn. It contains the elements of Four, Seven, and Two; the four figures in the sphere surrounded by the seven planets plus the elements of sun and wind SECURE yourself by establishing your boundaries and building the protective egg of spiritual energy all about you. The meaning of this suit is protection. Relax in the knowledge that you are secure.

You are now at a stage where you need have no fear of physical or metaphysical actions against you. You are well protected. Actions may take place nearby but you will remain untouched. The forces of the Sun and the Moon together, with five powerful planets, watch over you. You are now at a beginning stage in the process of passing on the knowledge you have acquired. The time is ripe to teach others; to breathe the spirit of your teachings into those who come into contact with you. The old man is the survivor of many years of conflict. He is now safe and secure; finally able to relax.

The angels that are soul and spirit are watching over him, while the raven of sudden, violent action is at his beck and call, now a servant of the master. The egg of protection surrounds and encompasses the man, keeping at bay all that would harm him. (Remember, the Egg of Protection is the symbol of this suit.) Outside, the elements battle: the Sun blazes forth with intense heat against the gale-force of the winds, directed in freezing intensity. Above, the Sun and Moon, in company with the planets, look on approvingly. Of the planets, Saturn is shown in its negative aspect.

Beware, therefore, of selfishness, meanness; of being narrow-minded and dogmatic. Of the numbers of significance apparent in the picture: Four is represented by the old man, the two angelic figures, and the raven. Four is the number of opposites. Although not signifying opposition per se, it does signify independent thinking. It is a practical number; the number of order and stability. Although you may enjoy being alone you may experience periods of loneliness and isolation, which, in turn, can lead I3I The Cards to despondency and melancholy at this time.

You may also have a hard time making triends right now, but those you do make will be fiercely loyal. Seven is frequently regarded as a "lucky" number. Seven indicates that now is a good time for richness of ideas. It is not a good time for travel, though plans for future travel may be made right now. Interestingly Two is frequently thought of as the companion to Seven; Two is the Moon and Seven is the planet Neptune, always associated with the Moon. Two is a sign of art and imagination. You may operate more on the mental plane right now; preferring the reading of things to the actual doing.

You need to guard against restlessness and may become frequently oversensitive. If not constantly uplifted, you can grow despondent.

Planetary conjunction: MOON-VENUS This is a time for relaxation and luxury; for enjoying hard-earned rest. Emotions are calm and gratitude should be shown for that. This is a card more favorable for men than for women, especially where family life is concerned. Women still have a tendency to fret and worry while men have arrived at the stage of complete ease and repose. Beware of too much self-satisfaction, and recognize those who have helped place you where you are. There is a great love of beauty and an appreciation of art. This is a good time to take up hobbies, especially those involving the use of your hands.

Beware of moodiness and don't be surprised to find dency to be overly assertive. An inability to fully express all your emotions. Fight against any

The topaz is found in a variety of colors: black, green, pink, white, and yellow, though white, yellow, and pink are the most common colors. The yellow topaz is worn for health, protection, and to gain knowledge. It is regarded as the jewel of nobility and regal splendor. Since the yellow topaz is associated with the Sun, the jewel is I32 Egg Suit also associated with courage and leadership, making you fearless and wise.

It is a stone of security and is also good for transforming you into a nobler self.

Grade: This card is in the Adept grade. This indicates that you have attained a degree of advancement where you are recognized as knowledgeable and experienced. Others will turn to you for help and advice, sincerely believing that you can help them. Don't let them down. Never be flippant in answering a question, even if the questioner seems offhand or even facetious. Your words carry weight. This does not mean that you must always be overly serious; you can be humorous and light yet still deliver practical, positive counsel.

name: Mature
description: A stag, symbolizing soul and Mercury, approaches a unicorn, symbolizing spirit and sulphur, in a forest representing the body. The unicorn has a golden horn and golden hooves, and a large pool lies behind the two figures.
narrative:
Mature asks power to become seasoned rather than merely forceful. Bravery is joined with the ability to learn and to teach: experience has value when it remains open, can be tested, and can be passed on without hardening into superiority.

The stag and unicorn meet within the forest-body. The stag carries soul and Mercurial intelligence; the unicorn carries spirit and sulphur. One appears in the unicorn's single horn, while Two appears in the stag's antlers and in the pair themselves. Maturity emerges as singular purpose learns to live in relationship.

The card's challenges—excessive trust, egotism, and loneliness—show what happens when power becomes isolated or unexamined. Mars–Pluto intensifies the will to transform; Agate steadies that force through grounded strength and balance. In the Puffer grade, the work is still experimental: learn by doing, and let every lesson make your power more responsible.

name: Subdue
description: A wild man rides and tames a unicorn. The unicorn rears from a rock on which it stands, while a long-legged bird occupies the ground below. The opposed wild man and unicorn embody harshness and uncontrolled force balanced against purity and innocence; the bird carries the colors of fire and water.
narrative:
The picture shows a wild man riding, taming a unif...corn. The animal rears up from a rock on which it stands. On the ground below is a long-legged bird. The wild man was a common figure in medieval times, particularly in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. Wild men may still be seen as supporters for the armorial bearings of such families as La Rochefoucauld, a sixteenth century German manuscript shows a wild man running with a small tree over a shoulder. Tied to the tree is a young man. Wild hairy men are sculpted into the main portal of the fifteenth century's church of San Gregorio, in Valladalid, Spain.

In many, if not most, of the medieval festivals across Europe, the wild man was a traditional figure. A fourteenth-century ivory jewel casket is carved with a scene of a knight in armor rescuing a maiden from a wild man. While the wild man symbolizes harshness, lust, and lack of control, the unicorn is the opposite, representing purity and innocence. Is the unicorn being subdued by the wild man, or is the wild man being subdued by the unicorn? There's plenty of balance of opposites, a dichotomy of rider and mount. Both may be viewed as wild and unruly, and both may need to be subdued.

The card indicates that there may well be a similar dichotomy within you, a wildness purity, a violence gentleness, which swings first one way and then the other. The combination of opposites is reflected in the bird, which carries the color of fire and water. Obviously, the concept of the union of opposites is important in this card. With natural hostility needing to be overcome and subdued. Then it could be overcome is obvious from the picture, where there is a balance and a mutual respect in evidence. Watch out for strong inner urges that you know to be unhealthy.

Know that you can subdue whatever may present itself. You have the inner strength to do what you know to be best for you.

Planetary conjunction: Mars, Uranus. Although you may tend to appear cold and impersonal to others at times, you have a strong personality and are very capable. At present, you must not let your heart rule your head. You need to be in charge, to examine your needs and desires, and to look forward to the possible consequences of your actions. This is a time of high, intense energy, which must be strict...which must be kept under strict control. You have the ability to make quick decisions, but would be advised to take more time than you think, necessary. You may balk against routine, but some routine is necessary.

Stone: bloodstone. The bloodstone, or heliotrope, is a variety of green jasper. It is called bloodstone because of the distinctive red specks with which it is impregnated. These are actually caused by the iron oxide in the stone. It reduces both mental and emotional stress. It can also promote the healer within you by stimulating the Kundalini. Bloodstone was worn as an amulet by the Gnostics, in the belief that it would prolong their life. Worn around the neck, it is said to stop nosebleeding, however severe. In your working to help others, wear the bloodstone as an amulet.

Hold it in your hand and concentrate your energies into it for three minutes or more, at least once a day. Also hold it when sending mental images to help others.

name: Diversify
description: A hermaphroditic figure marked Rebis stands upon a fire-breathing dragon. A serpent crouches on a winged globe below. The figure holds a square and compass while the seven planets extend around and connect to the body. Everything is enclosed in the alchemical egg, beyond which positive and negative forces pulse.
narrative:
Diversify invites you to widen your interests and listen beyond a single point of view. Restricting yourself too narrowly can close off opportunities; curiosity, adaptability, and openness allow the world's varied strength to move through you. The work is not to scatter your energy, but to marshal it and direct it with purpose.

Rebis—the double thing—embodies Two in One: opposites joined without erasing their difference. The square and compass bring discipline, measure, and useful limits. The seven planets surround and connect to the figure, representing the variety of influences that continually shape a life and the originality that can arise when those forces are consciously integrated.

The dragon is imperfect matter and immense potential: powerful, responsive, and dangerous when handled carelessly. Beneath it, the winged globe suggests completion already present in possibility. The square of Four and triangle of Three call for method, pacing, humility, and unity; the egg protects the work from uncontrolled positive and negative fluctuations so transformation can proceed in its own time.

Mars–Neptune supplies enthusiasm, imagination, and strong feeling, but it requires selection and direction. Avoid vanity, disappointment, chemical escape, and anxiety about what cannot be controlled. Jasper grounds the card's openness and change, supporting courage, steadiness, trust, and a sustainable pace. In the Puffer grade, experimentation is welcome—provided each experiment teaches you how to focus your growing power.

name: Execute
description: The key illustration is a great green lion with a Sun between its jaws and blood falling to the ground. The lion may be disgorging rather than devouring the blood and Sun. The secondary illustration is a dragon standing in a field near a tree stump, apparently at rest but alert.
narrative:
Execute is the keyword. It is the time to put plans into action, take charge and move forward, examine your current situation, weigh up the other card drawn with this wild card. Know that you have the elements of this card in reserve to use with or against the forces displayed in your other card, and execute accordingly. Fear must be slain, and you must face up to responsibilities. This card represents raw earth at your command, ready for you to execute. It is your trump card, literally, and that you have both lion energy and dragon energy at your call if you should ever need it.

Here's a chance to draw forth necessary power and strength. Here is a reservoir of opportunity. Use this power wisely and only when considered necessary. Take the time to sit and study this card, drawing on it for insight and inspiration. Let it help you develop your responsibilities and help you achieve a greater sense of self-worth and pride. Earth element, You're practical and stable, like the dragon, you have your feet planted firmly on the ground. It is from the earth, from the ground, you can most easily draw your power.

You can be tolerant, loyal, and diplomatic, but if riled, you can make a dangerous enemy. Deep within, you have the courage of the lion. Mercury correspondence:. Mercury is associated with the brain and the nervous system, with the intellect, with mental perception. It gives the urge to acquire knowledge and to share that knowledge with others. It shows excellent reasoning powers, perceptiveness and versatility, but can also make you argumentative, sarcastic, and cynical. Many of these positive traits and even the negative ones, can be used for good if handled wisely
